# Work-Thread Signal Audit (Step 1)

**Question this audit answers:** does Dataset A actually contain the *linking* evidence
a work-thread reconstruction needs — the kind of signal that says "this event and that
event belong to the same unit of work"?

**Method:** every `events.jsonl` in Dataset A streamed directly (162,768 events across
117 chunk files, 63 sessions). Coverage is measured as a share of all events, not of
the events where the field happens to apply — the optimistic denominator would hide
exactly the problem this audit is looking for.

**Generated by:** the audit scripts recorded in
`reports/day7/work_thread_reconstruction_analysis.md` §4. All figures below are
**OBSERVED**.

---

## 1. Coverage table

| Signal | Availability | Coverage | Example | Can it link two events? | False-positive risk | False-negative risk |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | Always | 100% | `ses_20260630-121953-…` | **No** — scopes, does not link. A session holds many executions | — | — |
| `timestamp_ms` | Always | 100% | `1751276393000` | **Weakly.** Proximity only | High — adjacent events often span a boundary | High — real pauses inside work exceed boundary gaps (Day-2: 2,627 ms vs 526 ms medians) |
| `event_type` | Always | 100% | `keystroke`, `app_switch` | **Weakly.** Compatibility only | High — every execution uses the same verbs | Low |
| `application` | Near-always | ~100% | `Microsoft Edge` | **Weakly** | Very high — one app hosts many consecutive executions | Low |
| `window_title` | Near-always | **99.61%** | `Theme M1 - Mixed Multi-Domain (HR / Finance / Ops)` | **Measured: no** | — | — |
| `browser_url` | Partial | **52.64%** | `http://127.0.0.1:5122/` | **Weakly** | Very high (see §2) | Absent in 47% of events |
| `browser_domain` | Partial | **52.61%** | `127.0.0.1:5122` | **Weakly** — effectively 3-valued | Very high | Absent in 47% of events |
| `tab_id` | Sparse | **5.74%** | `tab_2007116113` | **Measured: no** (see §3) | Very high | Absent in 94% of events |
| `target_field` | Partial | 23.86% | `{'automation_id': None, 'bounding_rect': {...}}` | **No** — geometry, `automation_id` is null | — | — |
| Extracted / screen text | **Effectively absent** | **0.07%** (116 events) | `operator2Nttd.co.jp` | **No** — nothing to overlap | — | Present for 1 event in 1,400 |
| Clipboard content | **Absent** | 0% of 5,198 clipboard events | metadata only | **No** — see §4 | — | Total |
| DOM element identifier | **Absent** | **0%** | — | **No** | — | Total |
| Entity identifiers (case/record/customer ID) | **Not observable** | **0%** | — | **No** | — | Total |

## 2. `browser_domain` is effectively a 3-valued signal

17 distinct domains exist across the whole dataset, but the distribution is extreme:

| Domain | Events |
|---|---:|
| `127.0.0.1:5122` | 30,759 |
| `127.0.0.1:5123` | 28,257 |
| `127.0.0.1:5124` | 26,145 |
| `www.nta.go.jp` | 133 |
| `www.nenkin.go.jp` | 105 |
| everything else (12 domains) | <100 each |

**99.6% of domain-bearing events fall into three localhost ports.** As linking
evidence this is close to useless: two events sharing `127.0.0.1:5122` tells you they
were both in the same internal system, which is true of hundreds of consecutive
executions. 56 of 57 sessions carrying domains have ≥2 distinct values, so the
*diversity* exists at session level and disappears at execution level.

## 3. `tab_id` exists but is 37.8× too coarse — **the most important negative finding**

This was the one genuinely entity-like identifier in the schema, so it was measured
carefully rather than dismissed.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---:|
| Coverage | 9,335 events (**5.74%**) |
| Sessions with any `tab_id` | 56 of 63 |
| Distinct tabs per session | median **3** (min 3, max 25) |
| Events per tab | median 47, p90 77, max 255 |
| **Tab lifetime** | median **1,197.1 s** (p90 1,523.5 s) |
| **GT execution duration** | median **31.7 s** (p25 25.9, p90 66.4) |
| **Ratio** | **37.8×** |

A tab is alive for roughly **38 median executions**. Two events sharing a `tab_id`
are therefore *very likely* to belong to different executions. The identifier is real,
but it identifies a long-lived browser container, not a unit of work. Using it as a
same-work edge would merge dozens of independent executions — the exact failure mode
(§9 of the research brief) that a false merge is supposed to avoid.

## 4. Clipboard carries no content — copy→paste chains are not reconstructable

5,198 `clipboard_change` events exist, and their payloads are:

| Payload field | Present |
|---|---:|
| `content_type` | 5,198 |
| `formats_available` | 5,198 |
| `text_length` | 5,193 |
| `source_action` | **4** |
| `binary_content_info` | 1 |

There is **no clipboard text**, and `source_action` — the field that would say what a
paste came from — is populated 4 times in the entire dataset. Day 1 recorded the same
finding independently (`payload.text_content` null in every sample checked).

A copy→paste relationship could in principle be approximated by matching
`text_length` between a copy and a later paste, but with only a length integer to
match on, collisions would dominate. **Not viable.**

## 5. Text / OCR overlap is not available

116 events out of 162,768 carry extractable text (**0.07%**), with median length 13
characters and p90 19. Token-overlap, entity-token overlap and normalised text
similarity — three of the features the research brief proposes — have **no data to
operate on**.

Note this is not the same as Day 1's `text_input_complete` finding. Day 1 corrected a
profiling bug and showed `final_text` is present for ~98% of *that event type*; this
audit measures coverage across **all** events, which is the denominator that matters
when asking whether an arbitrary pair of events can be linked.

## 6. Signals deliberately excluded from consideration

- **`window_title` (99.61% coverage).** The highest-coverage signal in the dataset and
  therefore the most tempting. It has been measured twice and rejected twice: Day 1
  put its boundary lift at **0.048** (it is *less* common at boundaries than
  mid-execution), and Day 4 re-tested it as a fallback at median lift **1.10**, firing
  at 3.33% of boundaries versus 3.55% of non-boundaries — at or below chance.
  Re-adopting it now without new evidence would be pattern-matching on coverage rather
  than on discriminative power.
- **GT-derived anything** — `process_code`, `case_id`, execution boundaries, execution
  length, execution event counts. These are the evaluation reference and may never be
  features.

## 7. What this means for the hypothesis — **INFERRED**

The work-thread model needs edges that say *"these two events are the same work."*
Ranked by what the data can actually support:

| Evidence class the hypothesis assumes | Status in Dataset A |
|---|---|
| Entity identifiers (case/record ID) | **Not present** |
| Clipboard copy→paste chains | **Not reconstructable** (metadata only) |
| Text / token / OCR overlap | **Not available** (0.07%) |
| URL family / deep-link structure | **Effectively 3 values** |
| Stable work-thread identifier | `tab_id` exists but is **37.8× too coarse** |
| Temporal proximity | Available, and already the dominant feature of the locked model |
| Application / window context | Available, already used, and window title measured ineffective twice |

**Every signal capable of *linking* two events across a gap is either absent or too
coarse.** What remains — time, application, event type, and a 3-valued domain — is
precisely the feature set the locked V1/V2 models already consume.

This does **not** by itself refute the hypothesis, and this audit does not treat it as
doing so. It predicts a specific, falsifiable outcome: a pairwise "same execution"
classifier built on the available evidence should perform **poorly at exactly the
distances where linking would be valuable** — across gaps, and across an intervening
different-work block (the A→B→A case). Step 5 tests that prediction directly rather
than assuming it.

## 8. Consequence for Step 2 (unit of analysis)

Because there is no entity, no text and no usable thread identifier, a "normalised
activity" node would carry no information a raw event does not already carry — the
normalisation would be over `(application, event_type, domain)`, all of which are
already fields. **Raw event is therefore retained as the unit**, with a bounded
temporal neighbourhood, and the decision is revisited in the research report if the
pairwise experiment says otherwise.
